candidates.decision_summary: Task1 passes all thirteen checks. The original paper studies observational individual-level immigrant wage gains from last home-country job to U.S. job and reports the focal education comparison. The authorized dataset contains one row per immigrant, adjusted home and U.S. wages, education years, and country; no person ID or repeated-measure panel structure is present beyond paired home/U.S. wage measures within the same individual. The code reads only the authorized wage_gain_table.xlsx, constructs log_wage_gain as log adjusted U.S. wage minus log adjusted home wage, defines education groups using the anchor cutoffs, keeps positive finite wages, includes country fixed effects, estimates OLS with HC3 covariance, and writes JSON, sample-flow CSV, and model-summary outputs. No low-quality rule is triggered: there is no materially different estimand under Rules 1.1 or 1.2, no unsupported focal variable under M2, no undocumented exclusion under M3, no unjustified material control under M4, and identifiable executable code is present under Rule 1.4. Guardrails G1, G8, G9, and G14 were considered for possible alternative model or uncertainty preferences; none supplies a basis for rejection.
